cart.discountBasisSubtotalSelectorComment: Hyva renders one subtotal row, so the discount is measured against the same node as subtotalSelector. Core's default is Luma-shaped (tr.totals.sub...), which matches nothing here — this override is required, not cosmetic.

productPageComment: priceSelector: Hyva renders the MAIN product's price through its own Alpine `initPrice` component, which emits `.price-box > div > .price-container > .final-price > .price-wrapper > .price` and drops the `data-price-type="finalPrice"` attribute core's selector keys on (the listing tiles further down the page keep it, which is why the scope to `.product-info-main` is not enough on its own).
comparePageComment: Hyva's comparison table carries neither an id nor a class of its own; it is the only table in the main column, which is what makes this unambiguous. Every other comparePage handle is core's and resolves identically inside it.
reviewFormComment: Hyva stacks the star inputs behind their labels without giving them ids, so the star is addressed by its accessible name instead of by Luma's `#Rating_<n>`. `%s` is the star count - note '1 star' is singular, which is why the tests use 5.
minicartComment: itemPriceSelector: the cart drawer renders each line's price as a bare `.price-box` injected with `x-html`, with none of Luma's `.product-item-pricing` wrapper. Resolved inside the line's own row by the page object, so the drawer's own Subtotal (which sits outside every row) cannot satisfy it.
orderViewPageComment:
Hyva's order view drops Magento's `.box-order-billing-method` class and labels each box with a plain `

`, so the payment-method box can only be told apart from the shipping-method box beside it by that label. The `> p` is a DIRECT child, which is what keeps the match to the one wrapper. A translated storefront overrides this whole string.
